entities.name: Nagarjuna
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Indian Buddhist philosopher (c. 150–250 CE), founder of the Madhyamaka ("Middle Way") school and arguably the most important Buddhist thinker after the Buddha himself. His masterwork, the Mulamadhyamakakarika (Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way), systematically demonstrates through rigorous dialectical analysis that all phenomena are "empty" (shunya) of inherent existence — arising only through dependent origination (pratityasamutpada).

His doctrine of two truths (conventional and ultimate) and his tetralemma (catuskoti) method of logical analysis profoundly shaped all subsequent Buddhist philosophy in India, Tibet, China, Japan, and Korea. The Dalai Lama has called Nagarjuna the most important Buddhist philosopher in history.
